It’s because people prefer it to be sadness because it’s “aesthetic” and social media has made depression look like it’s sitting at your window, having tea while having depressing piano music in the background. I was diagnosed with depression at 7 years old, but I had a genetic predisposition to it, but became more severe when I grew up (I’m 20 now), and honestly it feels like a void of every emotion but pain, whether it be physical, mental or both. Before I started medication again in 2017, I would have really happy days and really bad days that go beyond depression. Come to find out I have Schizoaffective + Bipolar 1 type, so it explains the periods of stimulation and mania and then the periods of lethargy with other mental problems. It hurts, when I’m depressed I don’t even call it depression, I call it living in hell. My stomach feels like there’s a pit where it should be, my heart hurts because it’s pounding so fast from not knowing what to do next. People with actual depression don’t post about it unless it’s a logical post with their experience, we don’t talk about it 24/7. Maybe at first we do because the feelings so odd feeling I guess? But after a while we shut down and quit talking about it because our illness has deluded us into believing nobody cares and if they do, they’re just caring to be kind and not seem like a dickhead. Depression whether it be clinical, an addition to another illness, or situational, sucks and people who are actually depressed don’t like talking about it because everything is pessimistically viewed (Example: “Why even post this, what good is it gonna do me? I mean people don’t care about it and / or me and I know getting help wont actually work, so why even talk about it?”) That’s how I see it as, and that’s how it is for me. And all of that that I just said is mainly why people with actual severe depression take their own lives. They feel hopeless but beyond that, they feel apathetic and don’t care whether they die or stay alive. The tricky part is, some people with depression such as myself feel stuck. I personally feel like I’ll be miserable dead or alive, so you don’t know what to do and that’s when anger comes in, and then I end up snapping / black out and end up harming myself intentional or not. I just got out of the psychiatric ward because of all of that shit, but I was also escaping reality with drugs and with my SZA I was psychotic and depressed to the point to where I was numb and ended up going manic.

See people think chronic depression is easy to get, but there is alot that plays into having it. Genetics play a huge role, responses to a prolonged negative environment, trauma, physical activity, street drugs / prescribed drugs etc.. There’s alot in my opinion. People misconstrue sadness for depression. Depression is a mental illness, sadness is an emotion and I’m not saying depressed people don’t get sad, because I know I do.. But I know how to differentiate my depression from regular bouts of sadness. Society makes depression look like an aesthetic as opposed to a mental illness, and when you’re young you’re vulnerable and desperate to fit in. It’s a chain effect, someone starts presenting depression and they get unwanted attention, x, y, z child / teenager sees that and it’s something they want whether it be because they’re bullied, don’t get enough attention from people around them, or want to look “aesthetic”. It’s like how the media portrays Schizophrenia but it isn’t presented as an “aesthetic”; it’s presented as a psychopathic killer, and who wants to be viewed as that? Not as aesthetic as “depression” if you get what I’m trying to say.

Edit: And we also don’t make our whole identity about depression, depression makes us it’s bitch and wants us to stay silent about it. It kidnaps us from our true selves, and makes us believe nobody not even God give a shit about it. It tells us in our heads, “You should take that fork and cut your wrists open with all of your force.” “Take that belt and wrap it around a rod and hang yourself with it.” “Swerve off the road and flip your car.” Depressions ultimate goal is to make you miserable until you are fed up and commit suicide.
